text:
harry_sales: Heads-up — BlueRidge POC is seeing 429s during a joint demo where they run a bulk-embed job + live personalization chat. Started ~11:02 PT.

harry_sales: Client error: `HTTP 429 Too Many Requests` with headers: `X-RDX-Limit: 15000`, `X-RDX-Remaining: 0`, `Retry-After: 5`. They report it persists even after standard backoff.

tanvi_se: Thanks. Can you share their request pattern? batch sizes, concurrency, SDK version?

harry_sales: Test script: 8 parallel embed workers, batch_size=256, and 10 concurrent chat calls. Using rdx-python 0.8.9.

ralph_backend: Quick theory: per-route accounting + streaming finalization spike from older SDK could produce surprise token spikes. Also per-route caps make it harder for the client to reason about "remaining" if routes drain a shared burst.

anya_support: Console snapshot for tenant=blueridge: tier=poc burst_window_s=60 burst_tokens=15000 window_used=14940 monthly_commit=50k

quota_bot: [quota-alert] tenant=blueridge used=14940 limit=15000 window=60s burst_remaining=60

tanvi_se: With ~60 tokens left, a single embed request at that batch size will overflow. Two quick customer-facing mitigations: 1) reduce embed batch to 64 and cap workers to 4, 2) request a short-lived burst reservation so the demo completes.

harry_sales: Customer prefers not to change code during the live demo. Can infra do a short bump?

ralph_backend: We can issue a 90m reservation: id=resv-20260321-7001 amount=8000 ttl=5400 scope=burst. Need sales approval and we log it.

harry_sales: Approve 90m reservation. Please note in deal and revert after.

quota_bot: [reservation] applied tenant=blueridge id=resv-20260321-7001 applied_by=ralph_backend expires=1766679721

anya_support: After reservation + ask to throttle down a bit, customer confirmed demo completed. They asked for concrete guidance to avoid this in future.

tanvi_se: Two short-term runbook items for presales: (A) preflight token estimate call before big imports, (B) basic client checklist: SDK >=0.9.0, embed batch <=64, parallel workers <=4, exponential backoff + jitter, and preflight for large imports.

harry_sales: Can we give them a tiny preflight helper snippet they can run in CI?

tanvi_se: Draft preflight example (estimate tokens for a file):
```bash
# estimate tokens for embeddings file
python rdx_preflight.py --file big.csv --estimate-by=items --chunk-size=64
# returns estimated_tokens and suggested_chunks
```

ralph_backend: Follow-ups for infra/SDK: 1) add an API endpoint `POST /v1/preflight` that returns estimated_token_cost and suggested_chunk_size (opt-in), 2) add aggregated header `X-RDX-AggregATE-REMAINING` so clients see tenant-wide remaining across routes, 3) SDKs to surface a warning if estimated request cost > current aggregate remaining.

anya_support: I'll add a one-pager to presales runbook and attach to the deal: quick checklist + the split/upload helper.

runbook_bot: [runbook-create] created runbook draft id=rb-20260321-42 path=presales/poc-embed-best-practices.md

tanvi_se: Small engineering note: we observed race conditions where concurrent requests read the same positive remaining and both proceed, pushing bucket negative. Propose an atomic test-and-decrement in proxy for token accounting and a "soft-fail" header that suggests aggregate remaining. Filing INFRA ticket INFRA-901.

ralph_backend: Filed: INFRA-901 (atomic accounting) and RUNTIME-2250 (aggregate header + preflight API). SDK teams cc'd.

harry_sales: Nice work — customer happy and POC green. Please add runbook link to CRM and mark the reservation in the deal notes. Thanks team! :white_check_mark:
